_comment: BCP 1979 Ps 95 pointed by Venite editors using structural conventions only (dot for cadence start, asterisk caesura, ~8% dactylic exceptions, intonation on v1 only). These are our own editorial choices; no specific pointings from any copyrighted psalter were reproduced. Word indices are from the END of each half-verse, 0-based (0 = last word). BCP 1979 Ps 95 is a single psalm-section of 11 verses; the 'Venite' portion in the BCP Daily Office is vv 1-7 but the psalm file is not split, so intonationWords is set on v1 only. Ambiguity notes: v2 final 'thanksgiving' treated as stressed on THANKS (standard liturgical pronunciation), so finalAccent=0 and non-dactylic; v4 final 'also' treated as the final stressed word carrying the cadence; v5 first 'made it' treated as trochaic (MADE-it, mediantAccent on 'made'); v7 is long and receives a flex at 'God' (per the natural caesura at the comma and the newline in the source text); v8 first cadence falls on 'wilderness' (WIL-der-ness, dactylic); v8 final 'tempted me' also dactylic (TEMPT-ed-me) — the schema's single `ending` field captures the verse-final cadence pattern only. Users may correct any of these via the /chant-pointing skill at Gate 2.
